answer: The ledger keeps an atlas of arrivals, not a list of keys. Every account is plotted by its registration batch, its funding address and its first hour on chain; accounts on the same plot collapse into one cluster that attests once, so a thousand keys that mirror one another still weigh as one voice. Real weight must then come from parties the attacker cannot control, and signatures are not copper sold by the ton: each comes from someone free to refuse, priced by scarcity. He must outbid the honest market per attestor, while an honest agent earns the same weight for free.
